[...] ietly became the default. Only zero selects the default.
- [`fc05013`](https://redirect.github.com/posthog/posthog-go/commit/fc05013): Send `PostHog-Request-Timestamp` and `created_at` with sub-second precision. Whole seconds made PostHog's clock-skew correction move events up to a second later. The batch debug log no longer prints each message.
- [`fc05013`](https://redirect.github.com/posthog/posthog-go/commit/fc05013): Default capture retry waits now vary randomly by up to 25% either way, so clients that fail together do not all retry at the same moment.
- [`fc05013`](https://redirect.github.com/posthog/posthog-go/commit/fc05013): Fix a data race between `Enqueue` and `Close`, and report capture failures that previously reached no `Callback` as one aggregate log line per batch.
- [`fc05013`](https://redirect.github.com/posthog/posthog-go/commit/fc05013): Event `timestamp`, batch `created_at` and the `PostHog-Request-Timestamp` header always carry 3, 6 or 9 fractional-second digits in UTC, for example `2025-01-02T03:04:05.000Z`. Before, Go trimmed trailing zeros, so a whole second had no fraction. Finer precision from your timestamp or the clock is kept.

</details>
